title: Global Semiconductor Sales Increase 6.4% Month-to-Month in July
gist: The Semiconductor Industry Association reports global chip sales hit $146.8 billion in July 2026, up 6.4% month-to-month and 135.1% year-over-year, marking the 17th straight month of MoM growth and the highest-ever annual sales total reached just seven months into the year.

insights.claim: Global semiconductor sales reached $146.8 billion in July 2026, up 6.4% from the June 2026 total of $137.9 billion.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A direct, current read on global chip industry momentum, a key macro input for semiconductor equity and supply-chain positioning.
insights.quote: global semiconductor sales were $146.8 billion during the month of July 2026, an increase of 6.4% compared to the June 2026 total of $137.9 billion

insights.claim: July 2026 global chip sales of $146.8 billion were 135.1% higher than the July 2025 total of $62.5 billion.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A more-than-doubling year-over-year figure signals an extraordinary demand cycle (likely AI-chip driven) rather than incremental growth.
insights.quote: 135.1% more than the July 2025 total of $62.5 billion

insights.claim: The global semiconductor market grew month-to-month for the 17th consecutive month in July, and the industry reached its highest-ever annual global sales total just seven months into the year.
insights.speaker: John Neuffer, SIA president and CEO
insights.so_what: A 17-month unbroken growth streak plus a full-year record hit mid-year suggests the up-cycle is broad-based and durable, not a one-quarter spike.
insights.quote: The global semiconductor market grew on a month-to-month basis for the 17th consecutive month in July, and the industry has already reached its highest-ever annual global sales total just seven months into the year
insights.locator: John Neuffer, SIA president and CEO

insights.claim: Monthly semiconductor sales figures reported by SIA are compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics organization and represent a three-month moving average.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Understanding the 3-month moving-average methodology is essential for correctly interpreting the reported MoM and YoY growth figures rather than treating them as raw single-month numbers.
insights.quote: Monthly sales are compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) organization and represent a three-month moving average.

insights.claim: Sales into the Americas, Asia Pacific, and China continue to drive strong year-to-year growth in the global chip market.
insights.speaker: John Neuffer, SIA president and CEO
insights.so_what: Identifies which regions are the primary demand engines behind the overall sales surge, useful for regional exposure analysis.
insights.quote: Sales into the Americas, the Asia Pacific, and China continue to push strong year-to-year growth.
insights.locator: John Neuffer, SIA president and CEO

insights.claim: Year-over-year chip sales growth in July 2026 was 171.3% in the Americas, 134.9% in Asia Pacific/All Other, 123.6% in China, 85.2% in Europe, and 50.8% in Japan.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The Americas' outsized 171.3% YoY growth versus Japan's more moderate 50.8% highlights an uneven regional recovery, likely tied to AI-chip demand concentration in the US.
insights.quote: Regionally, year-to-year sales in July were up in the Americas (171.3%), Asia Pacific/All Other (134.9%), China (123.6%), Europe (85.2%), and Japan (50.8%).

insights.claim: Month-over-month chip sales growth in July 2026 was 9.2% in Japan, 8.7% in the Americas, 6.8% in Asia Pacific/All Other, 5.2% in Europe, and 2.9% in China.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: China's comparatively muted 2.9% month-to-month gain versus Japan's 9.2% suggests a near-term deceleration in Chinese chip demand relative to other regions, worth monitoring for supply-chain and export-control implications.
insights.quote: Month-to-month sales increased in Japan (9.2%), the Americas (8.7%), Asia Pacific/All Other (6.8%), Europe (5.2%), and China (2.9%).

insights.claim: The Semiconductor Industry Association represents 99% of the U.S. semiconductor industry by revenue and nearly two-thirds of non-U.S. chip firms.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Establishes that SIA's sales figures are near-comprehensive coverage of the industry, giving the reported growth data high reliability for market analysis.
insights.quote: SIA represents 99% of the U.S. semiconductor industry by revenue and nearly two-thirds of non-U.S. chip firms.
